title: A rate, not a gap: regression and how well a line fits

objectives.statement: Read a fitted least-squares line by stating its slope and intercept in the units of the measured data, explaining what a one-unit change in the predictor implies for the fitted response, and justifying the sign from the way the predictor was defined.
Compute a least-squares slope and intercept from summarised paired data, verify the result by an independent route, and report both values with their units.
Calculate the residual for a named observation with its sign, and diagnose from a residual plot whether the straight-line form is adequate, naming the pattern that would show it is not.

Interpret the correlation and the coefficient of determination for a fitted line in the terms and units of the data, and state at least two conclusions a high coefficient of determination does not license.
Distinguish a prediction made inside the observed range of the predictor from an extrapolation beyond it, and refuse a specific extrapolation with a reason drawn from the data.
Explain what a multiple regression means by holding another variable constant, read an adjusted coefficient as a sentence about people, and state what adjustment cannot remove.

scenes.title: A difference with no "per" in it
A line with units on both ends
Two things the line does not say
Holding one thing still while another moves
Clinical wrap-up: one patient, and a line built from sixty others
